canonical.name: A V-category on this page has a set of objects, not a proper class, so V-Cat is treated as a theorem schema rather than as a forbidden ambient category of all large enriched categories
This page fixes Kelly's composition order B(A,B) after B(B,C), rather than silently swapping the tensor factors in enriched composition

The hypothesis ladder is explicit: monoidal suffices for the basic V-category, V-functor, V-natural-transformation, and weak-Yoneda layer; symmetry, closedness, completeness, and cocompleteness are only added where the source actually needs them
A Cat-enrichment matches a strict 2-category only with a set of objects and small hom-categories; the unqualified slogan is false
The Ab-enrichment theorem is the track-closing payoff, and it depends on the tensor-product universal property over Z rather than on an ad hoc bilinearity convention
The semiadditive or CMon analogue is recorded only as a remark unless a direct source is supplied at authoring time

The weak and strong enriched Yoneda lemmas are distinct: the weak form is a set-bijection, and the strong form is a particular end that does not by itself construct an enriched functor category on a large source
A cotensor is not detected by a bijection on underlying hom-sets alone
There need not be constant enriched functors
Conical limits do not suffice in general, and the failure already occurs for V = Ab rather than only in exotic bases
This page proves change of base for lax monoidal functors and the underlying-category instance, but it does not build the deeper 2-categorical change-of-base theory Kelly explicitly declines
The enriched adjoint functor theorem here needs both an ordinary adjoint and tensor or cotensor preservation; tensoredness or cotensoredness alone is not enough
The enriched density theorem is scaffolded only with its stated smallness and existence hypotheses on the weighted colimit; no large-source functor category is smuggled into the notation
